claims.text: As-cast HfMoTaTiZr has a density of 10.21 g cm.
As-cast HfMoTaTiZr is a single-phase disordered BCC alloy.
As-cast HfMoTaTiZr has high strength at room temperature.
As-cast HfMoTaTiZr retains high strength at elevated temperatures, including approximately 1000�C.
The proposed compositional intervention replaces Ta with Nb equiatomically, converting HfMoTaTiZr to HfMoNbTiZr.
Replacing Ta with Nb will reduce the alloy density by approximately 10%.
The modified alloy will have a density of approximately 9.510.0 g cm.
HfMoNbTiZr will maintain strength comparable to HfMoTaTiZr at room temperature.
HfMoNbTiZr will maintain strength comparable to HfMoTaTiZr near 1000�C.
HfMoNbTiZr will maintain creep resistance comparable to HfMoTaTiZr near 1000�C.
The Nb-substituted alloy will retain a single-phase disordered BCC solid-solution structure up to approximately 1000�C.
The Nb-substituted alloy will have lattice distortion comparable to that of HfMoTaTiZr.
The Nb-substituted alloy will have microstructural features comparable to those of HfMoTaTiZr.
Nb has an atomic mass of approximately 92.91 g mol, whereas Ta has an atomic mass of approximately 180.95 g mol.
The lower atomic mass of Nb relative to Ta will reduce the overall alloy density.
Nb's refractory character will preserve phase stability in the modified alloy.
Retention of the disordered BCC phase and comparable lattice distortion will preserve solid-solution strengthening.
The predicted mechanical performance is limited to quasi-static loading at temperatures up to approximately 1000�C.

contradictions.description: A 10% reduction from 10.21 g cm would be about 9.19 g cm, not the stated target range of 9.510.0 g cm. That range represents only about a 2.17.0% reduction.

The hypothesis attributes the outcome to a single Ta-to-Nb substitution, but the intervention also introduces a 1200�C homogenization anneal. Comparing this material only with as-cast HfMoTaTiZr confounds the compositional substitution with the processing change.
